correctness.rationale: Exact conditional attachment probabilities give the terminal two-coordinate martingale decomposition. The predictable covariance has matrix entries p(1-p), bpq, b^2q(1-q); the leaf variance bound <=(j-2)/4 proves replacement q_j by E L_j/d_j uniformly in L1 for theta_n/n->c>0. The three Riemann integrals yield the stated closed U,K,V, and bounded triangular martingale increments guarantee Lindeberg. Cramer-Wold martingale CLT and strictly positive conditional category probabilities prove the nondegenerate joint limit. Exact rational enumeration for n<=7 and deterministic finite-covariance sums are rerun in verify_hoppe.py; their finite scope is explicit.

originality.rationale: The main asserted claim is the joint Gaussian limit under linearly growing theta_n, with explicit off-diagonal covariance. The full-text Leckey-Neininger 2012 paper limits all asymptotic statements to theta fixed, and Hiesmayr-Islak 2017 proves marginal statistics for fixed weight sequences. Neither supplies a joint linear-attraction regime. The exact mean of leaves and fixed-theta marginal CLTs, and the easy finite covariance derivable from the mean, are acknowledged prior context rather than novelty. Residual risk of an unlocated general multivariate result remains.
residual_risks: A general unpublished or as-yet-unlocated multivariate triangular-array weighted recursive-tree theorem might imply this result.
The historical priority of the bivariate joint limit requires independent expert confirmation.

value.rationale: The scale theta_n~cn changes root degree from logarithmic size (fixed theta) to linear size, while both root branches and leaves exhibit sqrt(n) fluctuations. Explicitly identifying a strictly positive joint Gaussian correlation addresses a nontrivial dependence problem inaccessible from either marginal CLT. The c-dependent full covariance matrix supplies natural fluctuation calibration for the first-generation family and leaf statistics and pinpoints the critical competition between distinguished-root and bulk weights.
